description: This horizontal bar chart, titled “Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs,” illustrates the number of conversations categorized by perceived deception level across four domains: Academic Collaboration, Recruitment, Academic Funding, and Journalism. The x-axis represents the “Number of Conversations,” ranging from 0 to 60 in increments of 10. The y-axis lists the four domains, each associated with three horizontal bars indicating the level of deception: red for “Deceived: Yes,” yellow for “Deceived: Partially,” and green for an unlabeled category (likely “Not Deceived,” though the legend’s third entry is obscured). In Academic Collaboration, approximately 36 conversations were fully deceived, 27 partially deceived, and 7 not deceived. Recruitment shows about 38 fully deceived, 24 partially deceived, and 6 not deceived. Academic Funding has the highest number of fully deceived conversations at roughly 65, with 4 partially deceived and 3 not deceived. Journalism features 15 fully deceived, 48 partially deceived, and 6 not deceived conversations. The chart visually emphasizes that Academic Funding had the highest total deception rate, while Journalism had the highest proportion of partial deception. The legend is positioned in the upper right, with clear color coding for “Yes” and “Partially,” though the third category’s label is not fully visible.
